entry.title: New work in Science Advances
entry.content: 🎉 Natalia’s paper is out in Science Advances here! Using lab and field experiments in Mexico, the team showed that the inceptin receptor (INR) in common bean does more than amplify the wound response: recognition of inceptin activates an herbivore-specific pathway that releases a distinctive volatile blend, recruiting predatory wasps that remove caterpillars from the plants. Thanks to collaborators Patrick Grof-Tisza, Carla Arce, Eric Schmelz, Ted Turlings, and Betty Benrey. Congrats Natalia, Brian, Woody, Tonio, and Ben!

entry.title: New work in PLOS ONE
entry.content: Brian’s paper on natural variation in INR is out in PLOS ONE here! Some common bean landraces are insensitive to the caterpillar peptide In11. Brian, Wes, Tonio, and Ava found that this variation tracks with the expression level of INR, linked to promoter variation, rather than with changes in the receptor’s coding sequence. Congrats Brian and team!

entry.title: New work in Plant, Cell & Environment

link.title: New work in Plant, Cell & Environment

entry.content: Natalia’s paper with Takato Imaizumi is out in Plant, Cell & Environment here! In cowpea, responses to the caterpillar peptide In11 are gated by time of day: daytime elicitation produces stronger late-induced gene expression than nighttime, and this gating is lost in plants with arrhythmic expression of the clock genes VuLHY1 and VuLHY2. Congrats Natalia!
